correctness.rationale: For every nonempty legal core-arrow subset, the core edges decompose into directed paths, and a path endpoint has precisely one available pendant arrow. Toggling that arrow gives a perfect pairing on each fixed-core fiber. Removing fibers by decreasing core size and within fibers by decreasing face size ensures that each lower face has exactly one coface, so every removal is an elementary simplicial collapse. Pendant-only faces form the join of n discrete two-point sets, exactly a sphere S^(n-1). Symmetry follows by factor-permutation signs. Reproduced 24 finite cases, 34,838 faces, 15,622 actual legal free-face pairs; finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Inspected the core definitions and substantive theorems of arXiv:2601.05670v1, arXiv:2208.04656v1, arXiv:2110.11206 and the complete public results of the two closest corpus claims. The new theorem concerns full bidirectional vertex-whiskering of arbitrary digraphs, whereas the closest published results concern bare bidirected paths/polygons, coherently directed sunlets with exactly one pendant orientation, or once-subdivided bidirected forests. A new elementary-collapse mechanism uses endpoints of every fixed legal core multipath and is not implied by those narrower input families. Multiple actual meaning-based result searches and an earlier-claim comparison found no exact or dominating statement. Unindexed equivalent work remains possible.
residual_risks: Semantic searches and accessible papers cannot prove nonexistence of unindexed equivalent results.
A broader unpublished theorem on vertex-whiskered digraph multipaths may exist.

value.rationale: This is a uniform infinite-input simple-homotopy stabilization theorem with an explicit constructive collapse for every finite directed core, irrespective of cycles, branching, reciprocals, or its original multipath topology. It identifies all integral homology and the natural automorphism character, and distinguishes the bidirected-whisker operation from single-oriented sunlets and subdivided forests. The object is motivated by recent bidirected-polygon work and the effect of pendant attachments on multipath homotopy; this is not a parameter substitution or finite tabulation.
